instruction: Bake Surface Noise into Sphere Geometry The opened `scene.obj` contains a ZBrush Tool whose first (and only) SubTool, named Sphere, is a smooth polygonal sphere of radius 1.0 BU centred at the Tool's origin, with roughly 15,000-30,000 faces. Every vertex lies at distance 1.0 +/- 1e-4 from the origin; there is no surface noise, no polygroups beyond the default, no UVs, and no polypaint. Using the opened OBJ in ZBrush, apply a mid-frequency procedural Surface Noise pattern to the sphere, bake that noise into the mesh as actual vertex displacement, and export the result as `C:\Users\user\Desktop\output.obj`. The exported `C:\Users\user\Desktop\output.obj` must satisfy: - Exactly one SubTool, still named Sphere. - The face count equals the input face count exactly. - The standard deviation of (|vertex - origin| - 1.0) across all vertices lies in the range [0.004, 0.05]. - The axis-aligned bounding-box diagonal differs from the input's by less than 2%. - The mean per-vertex Laplacian magnitude is at least 10 x the input mesh's value. - The mesh is manifold.
